factor: Zoning status of the best parcel in the cell
formula: allowed 1.0; case by case or smaller only 0.7; site-specific / not yet reviewed / special area 0.35; rezoning needed 0.1; METHOD v4 (26 Oct): zoning is a gate, not a score: allowed or case-by-case 1.0, site-specific 0.5, rezoning 0.1
data: Vancouver: parcels + 2026 tax report zoning; Edmonton: 2026 assessment zoning
source_and_date: Zoning rules: tool/index.html vanStatus, edmStatus (research notes 17, 18); Edmonton IH under 1.0 ha = case by case (Bylaw 20001 s. 2.140)
status: rules sourced; the 1.0/0.7/0.35/0.1 values are an assumption; v4: an easier zone no longer outranks better exchanges (J.B.: a site that fails the exchanges shouldn't rank high)

formula: site x 0.6 in Designated Floodplain (FCL 4.6 m) or Still Creek Floodplain
source_and_date: City of Vancouver floodplain data (supplied 14 Oct 2026)
status: layer sourced; x 0.6 is an assumption

formula: site x (0.7 + 0.3 x ready), ready = max(0, 1 - building cover of the cell / 0.5)
data: building outlines from the tool tiles, unioned per cell (built_cover.py)
source_and_date: Vancouver 2009 City footprints + 2022 LiDAR outlines; Edmonton City 3D Buildings roof parts and rooflines
status: cell-level, not lot-level; 0.5 cover = fully built and 30 % maximum cost are assumptions; an existing shell may be reusable, so the cost is capped; Blatchford homes since 2015 missing from Edmonton outlines

formula: sum over receivers of demand x max(0, 1 - distance / reach); scaled so the 95th percentile = 1 ; METHOD v2 (25 Oct): x the direct-route 'pays' factor = min(1, gas heat value / heat-pump cost): Edmonton 13.0/38.4 = 0.338, Vancouver 39.4/42.0 = 0.938
source_and_date: Reach: tool/engine.js:33 (RVO 2018). Demand: fuel bought for heating x 0.85 boiler (tool/cards.js heatEcon); homes 16.81 / 33.14 MWh (NRCan CEUD, engine.js:29); per m2 by type (NRCan CEUD 2023, cards.js:154); large buildings from make_bigrecv.py
status: sourced (the tool's own rules); linear decay is an assumption; v2 pays factor from checks/site_math (trust 60)

formula: v2: per network, pays(d) = min(1, value / (cost at edge + pipe_per_m x d)) x timing, d = metres to edge (0 inside), to 1,200 m; heat = max(direct term, best network). v1 was 1 inside any network, 1 - 0.5 d/1200 outside.
data: site_maps/networks_v2.json: class, status, value, cost, pipe_per_m, timing per network
source_and_date: checks/site_math/SITE_LEDGER_2026-10-25.md; checks/networks/*_inventory_2026-10-25.csv; Blatchford outline corrected to Bylaw C17943 Sch. A (strip SW of Airport Rd removed)
status: value and cost from the hand-checked ledger; steam = 0; planned x 0.5 (assumption); Blatchford valued at gas parity $13 like every Edmonton route (utility's real avoided cost unknown); pipe $3,500/m mid (assumption)

formula: max(0; 1 - distance / 2000)
data: CanVec transformer stations (Vancouver 18, Edmonton 28) + named in-service or project stations (planned West End excluded)
source_and_date: NRCan CanVec 50K (map years 1986 Vancouver, 1977 Edmonton); BC Hydro and EPCOR project pages (tool/substations.json)
status: old map years; no capacity data exists for either city; 2 km and 0.6 are assumptions

factor: EV charging demand where public chargers are few
formula: households within 1 km (95th pct = 1) x (1 - public ports within 1 km / 20)
data: Census 2021 households on the 100 m grid; NRCan public chargers (Vancouver 505, Edmonton 201)
source_and_date: Census 2021 (tool/census_*.json); NRCan charger locator 16 Oct 2026 (tool/ev_*.json); 1,000 m from tool/opps.js:117
status: 20 ports = served is an assumption; EV hub is speculative on the sheets

formula: energy x 0.5 inside the West End CPCN study area
source_and_date: BC Hydro West End substation CPCN (2025): no new feeder positions until about 2032
status: area sourced; x 0.5 is an assumption

factor: Cooling towers and water treatment systems within 500 m
formula: count of permits (cooling tower + building water treatment) within 500 m; 95th pct = 1

source_and_date: City of Vancouver water-system permits (16 Oct 2026); 500 m from tool/xecon.js:101
status: proxy for a cluster that could share blowdown treatment or reuse (Quincy-type); Iona Island WWTP (1000 Ferguson Rd, Richmond) not yet placed: needs coordinates

factor: Distance to Gold Bar Wastewater Treatment Plant (reclaimed water)
formula: max(0; 1 - distance / 5000)
data: Assessment parcel zoned PU, River Valley Gold Bar, 19.7 ha (53.56019, -113.41248)
source_and_date: EPCOR: Gold Bar supplies local industry with reclaimed water from a membrane recycling facility (epcor.com Gold Bar operations)
status: plant location inferred from the assessment parcel (check); 5 km is an assumption

formula: max(0; 1 - distance to an arterial / 500)
data: Vancouver public streets (Arterial, Secondary Arterial); Edmonton Road Network (Arterial)

formula: share of parcels within 1 km zoned industrial (Vancouver I-, M-, IC-; Edmonton IH, IM, BE); 95th pct = 1
status: proxy for recyclers and refurbishers: their locations are not yet in the project

factor: Schools to pass computers on to
formula: schools within 2 km; 95th pct = 1
source_and_date: StatCan ODEF v2.1 (2022) and city lists via the tool
status: the pass-on route is a Microsoft claim on the sheets; 2 km and 0.2 are assumptions

formula: add homes from the 2026 assessment roll with year built 2022+: Residential accounts = 1 home; Other Residential = gross floor area / 85 m2; people = homes x 2.564 (city census persons per household)
status: v2 only; 85 m2 per rental home is an assumption; Vancouver has no comparable post-2021 data in the project, so not corrected there

factor: People who could use what it gives
formula: population within 800 m; 95th pct = 1

factor: Homes right next to it (night noise)
formula: benefit x (1 - 0.6 x population within 150 m / its 95th pct)
source_and_date: Night limits 45-55 dBA by zone (people sheet)
status: no source sound level is in the project, so 150 m and 0.6 are assumptions

factor: Public uses the zone allows (method v3)
formula: people x (0.5 + 0.5 x uses); uses = mean of six kinds (community, assembly/entertainment, markets, food, child care, urban agriculture): 1 permitted/outright, 0.5 conditional or temporary only, 0 not listed
source_and_date: Edmonton Bylaw 20001 s. 2.120 BE (1.00), 2.130 IM (0.25), 2.140 IH (0.00); Vancouver district schedules s. 2.1 (2026): I-2 0.50, I-1C 0.58, I-3 0.50, FC-2 0.67. 'Arts and Culture Event' is at most 6 days a month (By-law amendment, Oct 2023), so counted as temporary
status: size caps (e.g. BE 500 m2 per use) not scored; zones needing a site-specific or rezoning decision set to 0.5 (neutral); the 0.5/0.5 split is an assumption

formula: mean of heat; energy; water; materials; people
